papers.title: Convergence of the quasinormal-mode expansion of the Kerr Green function
papers.abstract: Black-hole ringdown is usually modeled as a linear superposition of quasinormal modes, and fits to gravitational-wave observations increasingly include high overtones. However, the overtone sum does not necessarily converge: overtones are more strongly damped and thus decay faster in time, but their amplitudes in the Green function (the signal at an observer produced by an impulse at a source point) grow, so the mode description may break down before a finite time. We show that for a rotating (Kerr) black hole this time has a clear geometric meaning. For highly damped modes, the amplitudes grow exponentially with the optical distance from the source and the observer to a characteristic "bounce" radius close to the black hole, defined as the location where the mode amplitude is smallest. For one family of modes, the amplitudes are also suppressed the farther the source and observer sit from the equatorial plane. Rotation therefore makes the onset of convergence depend on direction as well as distance, extending the geometric picture from bounce radii to bounce surfaces. Combining these effects gives a sufficient condition for absolute convergence. For spin $a/M = 0.7$, we map how this time varies with source and observer position, and amplitudes computed numerically reproduce the predicted spatial dependence to better than one percent. These results set geometric limits on when the quasinormal-mode sums converge.

papers.title: An Efficient Method for Directly Integrating the Vlasov Equation in Collisionless and Weakly-Collisional Simulations
papers.abstract: We describe and test a new numerical method to solve the Vlasov/Boltzmann equation in systems with arbitrary levels of collisionality. The method combines recent ideas to evolve the distribution function (DF) directly in 6+1 dimensional phase-space in a manner which is Lagrangian in both position+velocity. The 'particles' of traditional Monte-Carlo/Particle-In-Cell/N-body (MC/PIC/NB) methods become mesh-generating points defining a volume partition, each of which carries a set of momentum-Lagrangian basis functions representing a local anisotropic momentum DF. The DF is then integrated between cells and bases via a higher-order reconstruction and Godunov-type method, evolving a 10 or 13-moment representation of each basis to ensure manifest mass/momentum/energy conservation. The method allows one to represent arbitrary DFs, including multiple independent streams but also collisional or phase-mixed or thermal distributions (unlike traditional 'moments' or waterbag/tessellation methods), and the cost is bounded to a modest multiplier of MC/PIC/NB costs. We provide an example implementation which uses a spatially-Lagrangian volume partition, second-order reconstruction, and simple set of bases which ensure constant cell masses and couple directly to existing MC/PIC/NB machinery, made public in the code GIZMO. We validate in a series of test problems, demonstrating manifest conservation, Galilean and translation and rotation invariance, and ability to represent complex DFs without spurious dissipation or instability. We discuss applications where this method can have advantages compared to traditional algorithms for simulations of dark matter, stellar, weakly-collisional neutral gas, and particulate/dust dynamics; multiphase/polydisperse flows; cosmic ray and radiation transport/hydrodynamics; and plasma physics.

papers.title: The low-luminosity state of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205
papers.abstract: Context. At low accretion rates, X-ray pulsars can develop a two-hump spectrum through the thermalization and Comptonization of cyclotron photons in an accretion-heated, strongly magnetized atmosphere. Sources with independently measured cyclotron-line energies, $E_{\rm cyc}$, are particularly important because they provide a direct estimate of magnetic field strength and allow the continuum shape to be tested against spectral formation models. Aims. We investigate the luminosity-dependent spectral evolution of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205 and constrain the accretion regime in its newly observed low-luminosity state. Methods. We analyzed three NuSTAR observations obtained during the 2023 and 2025 outbursts, corresponding to the high-, intermediate-, and low-luminosity states at $L_{3-79}\simeq5\times10^{36}$, $4\times10^{35}$, and $6\times10^{34}$ erg s$^{-1}$, respectively. We supplemented these data with Swift/XRT observations and performed broadband spectral analysis of all three states. Results. The high-luminosity spectrum follows a classical cutoff power law, whereas the intermediate- and low-luminosity spectra require two thermal Comptonization components to reproduce their two-hump shape. In the intermediate state, the cyclotron line, first reported at $\sim50$ keV in the high-luminosity state, lies on top of the high-energy hump. We interpret the low-luminosity state as representing stable accretion from a cold disk. IGR J06074+2205 thus joins the very limited sample of X-ray pulsars with cyclotron-line energies that have been observed with a double-humped spectral shape.

papers.title: \texttt{StochAXtic}: a JAX-Accelerated, End-to-End Differentiable Framework for Gravitational-Wave Backgrounds from Compact Binary Populations
papers.abstract: We present \texttt{StochAXtic}, a package for computing the dimensionless energy density spectrum $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ of the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by compact binary coalescences. Rather than sampling binary populations via Monte Carlo, \texttt{StochAXtic} exploits the \emph{scale invariance} of the waveforms: at fixed mass ratio, spins and tidal deformabilities, the waveform depends on the total mass only through the dimensionless combination $Mf$. This allows all computationally expensive waveform evaluations using \texttt{LALSuite} to be performed once and stored in a population-independent lookup table. The subsequent integrals over mass and redshift can then be recast as convolutions and evaluated efficiently using fast Fourier transforms. We further employ truncated singular value decomposition to compress the lookup table, reducing both computational cost and memory requirements. Once the table has been computed and cached, \texttt{StochAXtic} evaluates $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ in a few milliseconds, achieving a relative numerical error below $10^{-3}$ at frequencies up to $1$ kHz. Its results agree with those of \texttt{popstock} within the latter's statistical uncertainties. Implemented entirely in \texttt{JAX}, \texttt{StochAXtic} also provides gradients of $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ with respect to population hyperparameters, enabling its direct integration with gradient-based inference methods including Hamiltonian Monte Carlo.

papers.title: Probing the Macroscopic Imprints of Singularity Resolution: Polarization Diagnostics of Rotating ABG Black Holes
papers.abstract: Recent observations by the Event Horizon Telescope have revealed important electromagnetic information around the supermassive black holes $\text{M87}^*$ and $\text{Sgr A}^*$, providing experimental supports for investigating physics near the event horizon. In the absence of a complete quantum gravity theory, exploring the observational appearances and polarized images of accretion flows in regularized geometries, and seeking specific observational differences from Kerr black holes, is of value for understanding the singularity problem. Based on backward ray tracing method, this work investigates both the optical and polarimetric observational features of rotating Ayón-Beato-García spacetime with regularization parameter $Q$. It is found that, compared with the Kerr case, the parameter $Q$ leads to a significant contraction of the size of the inner shadow in the observed optical images. This contraction remains visible even after an illustrative Gaussian filter for images observed at a low inclination angle (e.g. $17^\circ$). In the polarized images, we focus on two observables, the electric vector position angles (EVPAs) and the depolarization regions, on the observer's screen. It is found that depolarization regions do not necessarily reside in the vicinity of the bright photon ring in images at high inclination angles (e.g. $83^\circ$), and a multi-branch structure can be observed. Furthermore, the distribution of EVPAs is insensitive to the regularization parameter $Q$ while the morphology of the depolarization regions can be impacted remarkably by $Q$. The results provide possible optical observable characteristics for the rotating regular spacetime.

papers.title: Search for UHE photon sources using direction-time clustering algorithms with a BDT particle discriminant
papers.abstract: Direction-time clustering methods for neutral particle searches are motivated by the possibility that ultra-high-energy (UHE) neutral particles are produced during flaring periods of various astrophysical sources. In this scenario, clusters of events correlated in both arrival direction and time would be generated, which, when observed, would indicate a neutral-particle flare, and a non-observation would provide upper limits on fluxes for point-like sources. Focusing on UHE photon searches, an improvement of the sensitivity of direction-time clustering methods by the application of different photon tags, such as the depth of the extensive air shower maximum (X_max), the lateral distribution of the total signal across an array of detectors (S_b), or a cumulative signal trace-based discriminant variable (C_t), is investigated. A Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) is used to combine multiple observables, by which photon tagging is optimized and photon/hadron separation is improved. The number of events required to identify a photon flare is thereby further reduced compared to using individual photon tags, across a range of flare durations. The possibility of extending the known and assumed PeVatron photon sources into the UHE regime by applying these clustering methods to existing and future observatory data is also discussed. The discovery of UHE neutral particles would mark the next milestone in multimessenger astrophysics, by which a new window onto the non-thermal universe would be opened.

papers.title: New Historical Guest-Star Candidates from Reassessed Chinese Records: Lunar Occultation of Planets
papers.abstract: Ancient Chinese records of lunar occultations of planets have been used to test planetary theories and investigate long-term changes in Earth's rotation. However, certain records contain identification errors whose origins remain poorly understood; we propose that some of these errors may arise from misidentifying guest stars, such as novae or supernovae, as planets. We analyzed 67 errata on lunar occultations of planets from Liu Ci-Yuan's (2015) monograph using modern ephemerides and the open-source Python package \texttt{occultsky}, publicly available on GitHub. Using recorded dates and dynastic capital coordinates, we constructed observing windows anchored at solar noon and extending by $\pm 1$ day. Each window covered the preceding and recorded nights because the date may be off by one day. For each of the 67 records, we cataloged the apparent right ascension and declination $(α, δ)$ at the midpoint of the Moon's visibility window on each candidate night. The band swept by the lunar disk confines a possible transient to a narrow region a few degrees across; these midpoint coordinates serve as proxies for the implied guest-star positions. The catalog supplies candidate positions rather than identifications, enabling remnant and compact-object searches to test the guest-star hypothesis directly. If associations are established, these records could become dated guest-star candidates, and their dates could anchor remnant ages.

papers.title: Low-state X-ray spectra of magnetized neutron stars: Probing accretion regimes in SFXTs
papers.abstract: Supergiant fast X-ray transients (SFXTs) are a subclass of high-mass X-ray binaries characterized by prolonged quiescent states, making them ideal sources for studying accretion onto highly magnetized neutron stars (NSs) at low rates. In this work, we present a broadband spectral analysis of three SFXTs: IGR J16418$-$4532, IGR J17544$-$2619, and IGR J11215$-$5952, using archival $XMM-Newton$, NICER, and $ NuSTAR$ observations. Joint spectral fitting of the NICER and $NuSTAR$ data for IGR J16418$-$4532 confirms the presence of a cyclotron resonant scattering feature (CRSF) at $\sim 50$ keV, implying a NS magnetic field strength of $\sim 6\times10^{12}$ G. We detect a cyclotron line at $\sim27$ keV in IGR J17544$-$2619, significantly higher than the previously reported energy of $\sim17$ keV, a difference that may reflect luminosity-dependent changes in the accretion flow. Using a double-Comptonization model, we identify the characteristic two-hump spectral shape in IGR J16418$-$4532 and IGR J17544$-$2619 at luminosities $\lesssim10^{35}$ $\rm erg\,s^{-1}$, indicating that this spectral transition is a universal feature of accreting magnetized NSs independent of the source type. Furthermore, the ratio between the cyclotron line energy and the intersection energy of the two humps in both sources is consistent with the empirical relation established in Be/X-ray binaries, suggesting that the overheated polar cap atmosphere model used to explain X-ray pulsars in low-luminosity states is also applicable to SFXTs. In contrast, IGR J11215$-$5952 shows a smooth single-component spectrum at all flux levels, which indicates a relatively weak magnetic field of the NS.

papers.title: Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing Analysis (BADMET)
papers.abstract: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) variability is widely recognized as a promising avenue for constraining black hole mass, yet its practical application remains limited. Although the correlation between black hole mass and variability timescale has been extensively investigated, finite observational baselines often lead to systematic underestimation of the timescale, thereby hindering reliable mass estimation for individual sources. To address this limitation, we develop the Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing analysis (BADMET), an extendable framework that provides black hole mass estimates by assimilating multiple mass-related parameters that include variability properties. We show that incorporating the variability timescale improves mass recovery in the simulated sample and enhances agreement with the reference masses in the observed sample, achieving uncertainties of $\lesssim 0.5$ dex even with a single X-ray observation.

papers.title: Cataclysmic Variables from XMM-Newton and eROSITA
papers.abstract: Cataclysmic variables (CVs) are interacting binaries where a white dwarf accretes material from a late-type donor. The most evolved systems, referred to as period-bouncers, host degenerate donors. We present XMM-Newton and eROSITA, which provide complementary views of the CV population. We summarize the capabilities of XMM-Newton for timing and spectroscopic studies, and its ability to characterize accretion geometries, magnetic field strengths, and short-term variability across magnetic/non-magnetic CVs. These data allow studies of individual systems, including magnetic period-bouncers with soft X-ray spectra and faint luminosities that offer insights into the late stages of CV evolution. We then present an overview of eROSITA as the first X-ray all-sky survey in the soft band since ROSAT, and its impact on population studies. The eRASS:4 catalog expands the known X-ray sky and will enable volume-limited samples of CVs, complete up to 500pc for standard CVs and up to 250 pc for period-bouncers. Cross-matching eROSITA detections with optical catalogs produced the largest sample of X-ray-selected CV candidates to date, that will refine X-ray diagnostic diagrams, reassess the demographics of magnetic/non-magnetic systems, and identify new highly evolved CVs. Finally, we describe ongoing searches for unknown systems, including CVs selected through probabilistic cross-matching with Gaia, and period-bouncers identified through a multi-wavelength scorecard. These efforts led to the discovery of new period-bouncers and a promising detached period-bouncer candidate, that could validate alternative models for the evolution of CVs. Together, XMM-Newton and eROSITA provide an unprecedented view into the structure, evolution, and demographics of CVs, with eROSITA laying the groundwork for future studies of compact binary evolution, the Galactic Ridge X-ray emission, and related phenomena.

papers.title: Temporal polarization properties of accretion flows into supermassive black holes: INSANE as an alternative
papers.abstract: Temporal variability and polarization provide unique diagnostics of the magnetic field structure and plasma dynamics in accretion flows around supermassive black holes. We investigate the temporal polarization properties of horizon-scale emission using general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations coupled with polarized general relativistic radiative transfer (GRRT) for three accretion states: Standard and Normal Evolution (SANE), Magnetically Arrested Disk (MAD), and an intermediate regime (INSANE). Fourier polarization-mode decomposition, through the ratio $|β_m|/|β_2|$, shows that MAD produces the most rotationally symmetric EVPA patterns, SANE the most asymmetric, and INSANE lies in between. The multi-scale temporal behaviour of the intensity is investigated using the Continuous Wavelet Transform and Hilbert-Huang Transform. Both methods identify localized oscillatory features associated with magnetic-flux eruption events in the MAD simulations. In the shorter interval examined, INSANE distributes its variability more evenly among several time-scales, while the SANE behaviour depends more strongly on the electron-temperature prescription. To quantify the spectral distribution, we define a fast power fraction $F_{\mathrm{fast},I}$ for periods of 80-200 $M$ within a broad band of 80-1500 $M$. Both methods give the smallest fractions for MAD; the ordering of state medians, INSANE > SANE > MAD, persists when the upper fast-band boundary is varied from 200 to 500 $M$. Our analysis demonstrates that combining polarization morphology with multi-scale temporal analysis provides a useful means of distinguishing magnetization states, supporting INSANE as a distinct observational alternative to conventional MAD/SANE for interpreting horizon-scale observations of M87$^{*}$ and related systems.

papers.title: Magnetic Flux Eruptions in Magnetically Arrested Disks: Magnetic Reconnection and Bubble Expansion
papers.abstract: Using a high-resolution GRMHD simulation of a magnetically arrested disk, we investigate the physical mechanism driving magnetic-flux eruption. The horizon-threading magnetic flux declines mainly in off-equatorial regions, whereas localized hot spots associated with magnetic reconnection appear near the equatorial plane around the onset of flux decline. A non-axisymmetric, magnetically supported low-density structure, which we identify as a magnetic bubble, expands radially and azimuthally within a pre-existing low-density channel in the filamentary accretion flow. Based on these findings, we propose a physical picture linking reconnection, bubble expansion, and horizon magnetic flux decline. The reconnection occurs in the pre-existing low-density channel, and may reconfigure the field and promote bubble expansion. Magnetic-pressure gradients provide broadly distributed outward support for the expansion, while magnetic tension contributes a localized outward force near the equator. Bubble expansion may limit gas replenishment, helping to maintain the low-density region and reduce the total pressure near the equator. This pressure reduction may facilitate equatorward electromagnetic energy transport. In the simulation, the polar electromagnetic energy flux reverses from poleward to equatorward near the onset of the horizon-flux decline. The equatorward transport is concentrated in the bubble sector and carries electromagnetic energy from the off-equatorial magnetosphere to the equatorial region. This energy supply may sustain localized reconnection and plasma heating as the eruption develops.

papers.title: Properties of Chromium and Manganese in Tycho's SNR with XRISM/Resolve
papers.abstract: The X-ray emission of young supernova remnants gives access to the composition and spatial distribution of elements ejected in supernovae. The emission from the ejecta provides crucial insights into the explosion mechanism, especially for Fe-group elements formed in the innermost layers of the star. The objective of this paper is to provide constraints on the supernova progenitor and explosion mechanism of Tycho's type Ia supernova remnant by studying the properties of Cr and Mn. The unprecedented spectral resolution of XRISM/Resolve allows us to detect significant emission lines of Cr and Mn in different regions of Tycho's supernova remnant, even at small scale, providing a much more precise spatial distribution of Cr and Mn with respect to previous measurements. Significant Cr and Mn emission lines are observed in the Fe bright northeastern-to-southeastern emitting rim, some in the center region, but none in the southern region. The observed mass ratios of Mn/Fe, Cr/Fe and Mn/Cr, are consistent with 1D delayed detonation models of near-Chandrasekhar-mass Type Ia supernovae and 1D pure-detonation models of 1 Msol sub-Chandrasekhar-mass progenitors. In both cases, the observations imply supersolar zero-age main-sequence progenitor metallicities. Overall the best agreement is found for models with a too high metallicity to be realistic for Tycho's location. This points to additional sources of neutronisation such as carbon simmering for Chandrasekhar mass progenitor. For sub-Chandrasekhar mass, double detonation models with a WD mass lower than 1Msol are suggested.

papers.title: QPO constraints on the rotating Fan-Wang spacetime
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate a rotating regular black hole described by the Fan-Wang solution, which arises from nonlinear electrodynamics coupled to gravity. We examine the motion of neutral test particles along circular equatorial orbits and derive the corresponding orbital parameters, including the angular velocity, specific angular momentum, and specific energy. By perturbing these orbits in the radial and vertical directions, we calculate the associated fundamental epicyclic frequencies. We then employ the relativistic precession model to interpret the observed quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs) in terms of these frequencies. We numerically determine the radii of the innermost stable circular orbits and perform Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations to constrain the spacetime parameters. Using observational and theoretical estimates of the black hole mass and spin parameter from the literature, together with theoretically motivated priors on the Fan-Wang parameter, we obtain the best-fit parameter values. The inferred black hole mass, spin parameter, and QPO emission radii are consistent with the corresponding estimates reported in the literature. Furthermore, the dimensionless Fan-Wang parameter satisfies $l/M < 8/27 \approx 0.296$, in agreement with its theoretical upper bound.

papers.title: Relativistic tidal excitation of g- and i-modes in neutron star binaries
papers.abstract: When the gravitational wave frequency of an inspiraling binary matches a normal-mode frequency of a neutron star (NS), the mode can be resonantly excited. The excitation transfers orbital energy to the star and shifts the phase of the emitted gravitational-wave (GW) signal, thereby providing a potential probe of the NS interior. However, estimates of this phase shift in the literature vary by orders of magnitude due to different approximations and formulations used in calculating the tidal coupling strength. We revisit this problem using a fully relativistic scattering formalism, which serves as our benchmark calculation and provides a gauge-invariant mode response together with an effective tidal-mode coupling strength. We calculate the phase shifts induced by the excitation of stratification g-modes, crustal interface i-modes, and hadron-quark interface i-modes, and estimate their detectability with Fisher-matrix forecasts for current and next-generation detectors. In our models, direct g-mode excitation remains below the detection thresholds, even for the strongest stratification considered. Crust-core i-modes at large shear speeds provide the most favorable prospects and crust melting can produce a substantially larger phase shift. Hadron-quark i-modes remain below the next-generation detection thresholds.

papers.title: Probing Velocity-Dependent WIMP Dark Matter Annihilation in Large-Scale Structure
papers.abstract: The unresolved gamma-ray background (UGRB) provides a promising avenue for probing the cosmological annihilation of weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter through its cross-correlation with large-scale structure (LSS). While most previous studies have assumed a velocity-independent (s-wave) annihilation cross section, many well-motivated particle physics models predict annihilation rates that depend on the relative velocity of dark matter particles. In this work, we develop a generalized halo-model framework to investigate the cosmological signatures of velocity-dependent WIMP annihilation. Parameterizing the velocity-weighted annihilation cross section as $σv_{\rm rel}\propto v_{\rm rel}^{n}$, we consider four representative cases corresponding to Sommerfeld-like (n=-1), s-wave (n=0), p-wave (n=2), and d-wave (n=4) annihilation. We show that velocity dependence modifies not only the overall annihilation emission but also the halo population dominating the signal, leading to distinct effective halo biases, redshift distributions, and angular clustering properties. As a result, different annihilation mechanisms leave characteristic signatures in the UGRB-LSS cross-correlation that cannot be captured by the overall gamma-ray intensity alone. As an illustration of the formalism, we perform a statistical forecast for the cross-correlation between the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) UGRB and the Two Micron All Sky Survey Redshift Survey (2MRS) galaxy catalog and derive the projected sensitivities to the velocity-independent annihilation coefficient for these four annihilation scenarios. Our results demonstrate that cosmological cross-correlations provide a powerful and complementary probe of velocity-dependent dark matter annihilation, offering a new avenue for constraining the particle physics of dark matter through its imprints on large-scale structure.

papers.title: Low-frequency Radio Observation of the Dark PeVatron LHAASO J2108+5157 Using uGMRT. II
papers.abstract: We present deep radio observations of the PeVatron candidate LHAASO J2108+5157 using the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT). Our observations reveal a persistent double-lobed radio source (\gmrtext) within the vicinity of the $\geq$100 TeV $γ$-ray emission region, with consistent morphology across 400 MHz, 650 MHz, and 1.2 GHz. No alternative particle accelerators, such as supernova remnants or pulsar wind nebulae, are identified in the region, making \gmrtext\ the most plausible counterpart candidate. We measure the flux and spatially resolved spectra of the source using multi-band radio data. The morphology remains stable across all bands, while a comparison of non-contemporaneous observations suggests possible flux variability. From the measured spectra of the lobes the inclination angle of the jet is estimated to be $86.57^{\circ} \pm 1.15^{\circ}$. The multi-wavelength spectral energy distribution is modeled reasonably well with a lepto-hadronic scenario.

papers.title: The Lives and Deaths of Red Supergiants
papers.abstract: Red supergiants (RSGs) represent a brief yet pivotal phase in the evolution of massive stars, encompassing the final stages of nuclear burning for many core-collapse supernova progenitors. Having expanded to 100 times larger than their main-sequence sizes, they occupy the cool, luminous extreme of the Hertzsprung--Russell diagram. Characterised by extended convective envelopes, complex and dynamic atmospheres, and, sometimes, substantial mass loss, RSGs play a critical role in shaping both their own evolutionary outcomes and the circumstellar environments into which they ultimately explode. Despite decades of study, fundamental aspects of RSG physics remain poorly constrained, including the mechanisms driving mass loss and the connection between observed RSG populations and the properties of Type II supernovae. Recent observational advances have transformed the field, revealing episodic mass-loss events, asymmetric circumstellar structures, and signs of rapid evolutionary change in individual objects. Alongside these advances, studies of Type II supernovae and their progenitors have raised important new questions about the final stages of massive star evolution, including the possibility of rapid changes in the years immediately preceding core collapse. Motivated by these developments, this review aims to describe our current understanding of how RSGs live and die, from their observed properties through to their role as supernova progenitors, and where that understanding remains incomplete.

papers.title: Current Accretion State versus Black Hole Mass: Imprints on Multiphase Gas in IllustrisTNG
papers.abstract: The coupling between AGN feedback and the multiphase circumgalactic medium (CGM) is central to understanding galaxy evolution. In a previous paper, we showed that the black hole mass ($M_{\rm BH}$) correlates negatively with cold gas mass in IllustrisTNG100. We now extend this to the Eddington ratio ($λ_{\rm Edd}$), which traces the current accretion state, using the same sample of 5089 central galaxies at $z=0$ under the same group-specific partial correlation framework, controlling for stellar and dark matter halo mass. We find that $λ_{\rm Edd}$ correlates positively with warm gas in star-forming galaxies ($ρ\approx 0.6$-$0.7$), persisting after jointly controlling for $M_{\rm BH}$, the mass in the other non-star-forming gas phases, and specific star formation rate. The $λ_{\rm Edd}$-cold gas correlation instead reverses sign, from negative in star-forming galaxies ($ρ\approx -0.32$) to positive in quenched galaxies ($ρ\approx 0.40$). Controlling for $M_{\rm BH}$ leaves this correlation essentially unchanged in all three galaxy types. Further controlling for the total gas mass in the other phases strengthens the star-forming correlation and weakens the quenched correlation to $ρ\approx 0.21$, which remains significant. These results establish the Eddington ratio as a phase- and type-dependent tracer of the gas-black hole connection: the cold gas reservoir records the integrated black hole growth, the warm gas in star-forming galaxies carries the signature of the current accretion state, and the sign reversal of the cold-gas correlation marks the transition between the star-forming and quenched regimes.

papers.title: Depolarization of Synchrotron Polarization in Magnetized Interstellar Media
papers.abstract: We numerically study three key depolarization mechanisms of synchrotron polarization, including wavelength independent depolarization, differential Faraday rotation depolarization, and beam depolarization, across subAlfvénic and superAlfvénic turbulent regimes. Using 3D MHD simulations and synthetic observations, we analyze their effects on polarization degree and power spectra. We find that (1) SubAlfvénic turbulence shows high but strongly suppressed polarization under Faraday rotation, while superAlfvénic turbulence remains low and stable; (2) Differential Faraday depolarization dominates in ordered subAlfvénic media. For disordered superAlfvénic regimes, beam depolarization dominates at high frequencies, while at low frequencies it saturates and differential Faraday depolarization takes over as the dominant mechanism; and (3) Depolarization significantly distorts spectra in superAlfvénic turbulence but weakly affects subAlfvénic cases. Our results provide a quantitative basis for correcting depolarization biases in magnetic turbulence measurements with radio polarization data.

papers.title: Theoretical Instability Models of Quasi-Periodic Eruptions
papers.abstract: The nature of the Quasi-Periodic Eruptions (QPE) is still not firmly established while the phenomenon probes the innermost part of the accretion flow undergoing dramatic changes. In this chapter we review the possibility that the observed rapid variability is caused by the accretion disk instability. We summarise the defining observational properties of QPE sources: time scales of recurrence, the amplitudes of soft X-ray flares, high coherence over many cycles, and comparatively modest time-averaged luminosities. We then translate these into constraints on the characteristic radius, accretion rate, and energy reservoir of the inner disk. We review the main classes of disk instabilities relevant to supermassive black holes: radiation pressure induced thermal/viscous limit cycles, magnetically mediated inner disk transitions, and coupling to disk winds that can produce the oscillatory behavior. For each scenario we discuss the required parameter space (black hole mass, Eddington ratio, viscosity prescription, and truncation radius), the predicted spectral and timing signatures, and the degree of fine tuning needed to reproduce the observed duty cycles and flare morphologies. We highlight key tensions, including the extremely soft spectra, short recurrence times compared with standard viscous times at tens of gravitational radii, and the weak or absent contemporaneous optical/UV variability in several systems. Finally, we outline observational tests that may help distinguish between instability driven and geometrical or orbital models: phase resolved spectroscopy to track the temperature evolution, searches for hysteresis in hardness-intensity diagrams, reverberation and absorption variability tied to winds, and long baseline monitoring to measure drift in period and energy output.

papers.title: VLA Observations of the Ionized Jet IRAS 16562-3959
papers.abstract: We present new high-resolution, high-sensitivity Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) A-configuration observations of the high-mass protostellar jet system IRAS 16562-3959 at 3.1 and 6.1 GHz. Our images resolve the five previously known jet components (OE, IE, C, IW, OW) into 21 distinct knots and sub-components, and reveal a new off-axis source, MW. Based on the dynamical timescales from previous works ($τ_{jet} \approx 620$ yr), the spacing and structure of the knots suggest episodic accretion with a mean interval between ejections of $\sim$32 yr. We find that source MW has a substantial increase in peak brightness relative to its marginal detections in previous observations. MW exhibits a spectral index of $α\approx -0.7$, characteristic of synchrotron emission from shock-accelerated relativistic electrons. Equipartition analysis yields a minimum-energy magnetic field strength $B_{me} \approx 0.4$ mG, and a minimum total energy $E_{me} \approx 4.4 \times 10^{42}$ erg. Archival 2MASS Ks data imply a total outflow dynamical age of $\sim$1400 yr, and together with a HST [FeII] 1.64 $μ$m map, the NIR data indicate that the fast jet is embedded in a wide-angle wind with a $\sim 36^\circ$ opening angle.

papers.title: A search for optical bursts from the repeating fast radio burst in the M81 globular cluster, FRB 20200120E
papers.abstract: We present a search for optical bursts from the repeating fast radio burst FRB 20200120E, which is located in a globular cluster of M81 and is the closest known extragalactic FRB. We observed FRB 20200120E simultaneously with the high-speed, quintuple-beam optical camera HiPERCAM on the 10.4-m Gran Telescopio Canarias and the Effelsberg 100-m Radio Telescope. We detected one radio burst of fluence $\mathcal{F}_{\rm R} = 0.14\pm0.01$ Jy ms during our observations, but found no evidence for corresponding optical bursts in the 11.98 ms frames. We find 5$σ$ upper limits on the optical burst fluence of $\mathcal{F}_{\rm O} < 1.8\times10^{-3}$ Jy ms (combined $u_s g_s r_s i_s z_s$-bands) and the optical burst energy of $E_{\rm O} < 5.4\times10^{36}$ erg ($r_s$-band), corrected for interstellar extinction. We compare our upper limit on the optical-to-radio fluence ratio $\mathcal{F}_{\rm O}/\mathcal{F}_{\rm R} < 0.013$ to various emission models involving inverse-Compton scattering in the magnetosphere or nebula of a highly-magnetised neutron~star.

papers.title: Super-Eddington Accretion onto Compact Objects: Theory Meets Observation
papers.abstract: We review candidate super-Eddington populations together with semi-analytic models and radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations, with the following conclusions: $\bullet$ Likely super-Eddington sources over a range of black hole mass show similar properties, including outflow on a range of scales, hard X-ray weakness, decreased emission from jets, and suppressed optical/UV variability. $\bullet$ Theoretical treatment of super-Eddington accretion predicts similar behavior across a range of methods and initial conditions, although interesting differences remain, particularly in the importance of magnetic fields. Numerical simulations produce a puffed-up inner disk with a funnel that grows narrower at higher mass accretion rate. Radiative efficiency declines with accretion rate in thermal-pressure--supported disks. $\bullet$ Ubiquitous outflow is likely an important ingredient in galaxy feedback at high Eddington ratios, as wind mechanical power increases with accretion rate and can rival jet power. Wind kinetic power depends far less on uncertain black hole spin and magnetic fields. $\bullet$ Observational classes of objects can be sorted in a two-dimensional parameter space of Eddington ratio and orientation. Observations down the funnel observe rapid X-ray variability, while observations through the wind will see suppressed X-ray emission. At the highest Eddington ratios, we envision a regime where the photosphere extends to $r > 10^6 \, r_g$, and the observer sees only thermalized emission covering most of the sky, speculatively corresponding to super-soft sources and Little Red Dots.

papers.title: Long-Term Spectral and Timing Variability of PKS 2155$-$304 from {\it Chandra} and {\it NuSTAR} Observations
papers.abstract: Blazars exhibit strong variability across the electromagnetic spectrum, on timescales from minutes to decades. We present a study of the spectral and timing variability of the TeV blazar PKS~2155$-$304 using {\it Chandra} and {\it NuSTAR} observations spanning 25 years (1999$-$2024). Timing analysis reveals fractional variability amplitudes of up to $F_{\rm var}\approx 24\%$ in the hard X-ray band and $F_{\rm var}\lesssim 7.5\%$ in the soft X-ray band, along with variable power-spectral indices across observations. The minimum variability timescale, $τ_{\rm var} = 1.15\pm0.26$~ks, limits the size of the X-ray emitting region to $R \lesssim 7.7 \times 10^{14}$~cm, consistent with synchrotron emission from a compact region in the jet. We fitted the spectra using power-law (PL), broken power-law (BPL), log-parabola (LP), and bremsstrahlung plus power-law (BR+PL) models, the latter used only as a phenomenological description of the spectral curvature. The BPL model provides the best statistical description for most {\it Chandra} spectra. An F-test confirms a curved model over PL for all {\it Chandra} spectra, whereas most {\it NuSTAR} spectra are consistent with a single PL. Hardness ratio analysis shows a harder-when-brighter trend in the {\it Chandra} band. Joint fitting of the simultaneous 2013 {\it Chandra} and {\it NuSTAR} observations shows that the broadband 0.4$-$79~keV curvature is confined to the soft X-ray band, with the spectrum steepening above $\sim$2~keV and a steep hard X-ray power law ($Γ\simeq 2.7$). Our results reveal energy-dependent X-ray variability over more than two decades, and show that broadband X-ray coverage is needed to locate the curvature of the synchrotron tail in high-synchrotron-peaked blazars.

papers.title: Neutron-Rich Disks, Nickel-Rich Ejecta: Can Direct-Horizon Collapsars Explain Early $r$-Process Enrichment?
papers.abstract: Very massive stars above the pair-instability mass gap may collapse directly into black holes surrounded by massive disks. These "direct-horizon collapsars" accrete at $\dot{M} \gtrsim 10\,M_\odot\,{\rm s}^{-1}$ and have been proposed to eject a substantial amount of $r$-process material, powering "super-kilonovae". We present the first three-dimensional general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations of direct-horizon collapsars with M1 neutrino transport, following a $\approx 150\,M_\odot$ helium core from collapse through the escape of magnetically driven outflows. Extreme accretion rates neutronize the disks to $Y_{\rm e} \approx 0.1$-$0.25$ and, at early times, allow them to satisfy the gravitational-instability and cooling criteria for fragmentation. However, the strong poloidal fields needed to eject the neutron-rich gas promptly also drain the disks and lift their electron degeneracy. The neutron-rich ejecta composition is set in a brief phase, such that the ejecta carry $\sim 0.1$-$0.3\,M_\odot$ of nuclei with $A \geq 69$, including $\lesssim 2\times10^{-4}\,M_\odot$ of lanthanides, alongside $\sim 1$-$4\,M_\odot$ of $^{56}$Ni. Assuming proportional retention and mixing of Eu and Fe, these yields imply $[{\rm Eu/Fe}]\approx-0.4$ to $+0.3$, and simple dilution estimates permit enrichment at $[{\rm Fe/H}]\lesssim-2.6$. Direct-horizon collapsars are therefore potential prompt contributors to iron and $r$-process enrichment at low metallicity. Their predicted Eu/Fe ratios fall below those of strongly $r$-process-enhanced stars, but uncertainties in the relative yields, particularly of iron, may close this gap. The ${}^{56}{\rm Ni}$-rich ejecta would power luminous supernovae with rise times of weeks, potentially accompanied by exceptionally powerful gamma-ray bursts, rather than lanthanide-rich super-kilonovae.

papers.title: Mapping the multimessenger horizon for $γ$-ray counterparts of cosmic neutrinos
papers.abstract: The joint detection of high-energy neutrinos and $γ$-rays offers a powerful probe of the most energetic astrophysical accelerators, linking hadronic interactions to observable signatures across cosmic distances. Understanding the conditions under which these two messengers can be simultaneously observed is essential for identifying and characterizing the sources of cosmic neutrinos. In this work, we examine the detectability of $γ$-ray cascades associated with neutrino production in source environments that are gamma-ray transparent, focusing on how electromagnetic cascades evolve as $γ$-rays propagate through intergalactic space. By modeling photon interactions with the extragalactic background light and deflections in intergalactic magnetic fields, we determine the minimum neutrino fluence for transient emission and neutrino flux for steady emission required to produce a $γ$-ray counterpart detectable by $γ$-ray observatories, such as Fermi-LAT, HAWC, or LHAASO. This defines a ``multimessenger horizon" -- the region in flux-distance parameter space where neutrinos and $γ$-rays are jointly observable. We consider both energy-binned injection tied to IceCube's sensitivity and a continuous power-law spectrum extending from TeV to PeV energies. Our results reveal that detectability depends strongly on redshift, magnetic field strength, and photon energy, with higher-energy cascades suffering greater attenuation inside filamentary structures. The framework provides new constraints on source opacity, baryon loading, and neutrino production mechanisms, offering a predictive tool for interpreting current events and guiding future multimessenger campaigns.

papers.title: Flash UV Spectroscopy: Decoding the Ultraviolet Diversity of Young Core-Collapse Supernovae with the Hubble Space Telescope
papers.abstract: We present multi-wavelength observations and modeling of the largest sample to date of core-collapse supernovae (SNe) with Hubble Space Telescope (HST) ultraviolet (UV) spectroscopy within < 2 weeks of first light. Our total sample contains early-time UV spectroscopy from 12 Type II SNe (SNe II), 3 Type IIb SNe (SNe IIb), 3 Type IIn SNe (SNe IIn) and 1 Type I super-luminous SN (SLSN-I). This sample includes 11 objects with unpublished UV spectroscopy from HST Cycles 31 and 32 "Flexible Thursdays" target of opportunity programs, increasing the number of core-collapse SNe with early-time HST UV spectra by a factor of 2.4. The early-time near-UV spectra of most sample SNe II show similar Doppler-broadened P-Cygni profiles of metals (Mg, Fe, Ti, Cr), though with notable diversity in line velocities and absorption strengths. Comparison to non-Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (nLTE) radiative transfer model grids at similar phases indicates that most sample SNe II are consistent with low circumstellar material (CSM) densities at the time of UV observations (e.g., $\dot M = 10^{-6}$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$, $v_w = 50$ km/s) and standard kinetic energies (e.g., $E_k = 0.6-1.2$ B), while two objects, SNe 2024faq and 2023ixf, show UV/optical evidence for interaction with more confined, higher-density CSM. SN 2023ixf and sample SNe IIn exhibit relatively featureless early-time UV spectra despite displaying prominent optical Lorentzian emission lines from electron scattering in optically thick CSM -- this being attributed to differing properties of UV resonance versus optical recombination transitions as well as intrinsic CSM asymmetries. These results demonstrate the potential of early-time UV spectroscopy to constrain the outermost SN ejecta structure, explosion energetics/composition, and progenitor mass-loss histories of core-collapse SNe.

papers.title: Active Galactic Nuclei as Beyond the Standard Model Laboratories: a White Paper
papers.abstract: Multi-messenger and multi-wavelength observations of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) can provide otherwise inaccessible knowledge about physics Beyond the Standard Model (BSM), and may even lead to its discovery. Realizing this potential hinges on two parallel efforts: advancing our understanding of AGN and of the dark matter around them, and identifying the BSM signatures that are at once promising and robust against the gaps in that understanding. These fields have attracted growing interest in recent years, also motivated by the IceCube association of neutrinos to individual AGN, yet we have only begun to explore their cross-fertilization. This white paper offers a new perspective on this interdisciplinary endeavor. It concisely reviews the state of the art in each field and at their interface, and identifies the key open questions that must be addressed to strengthen our prospects for learning about BSM physics with AGN.

papers.title: Shocks and Trails in the Circumgalactic Medium Driven by Runaway Supermassive Black Holes
papers.abstract: Runaway supermassive black holes (SMBHs) have long been predicted. RBH-1, discovered with HST and confirmed by JWST, provides the strongest evidence yet for a runaway SMBH: a bow shock and linear trail in the circumgalactic medium (CGM) of a $z=0.96$ galaxy. The bow shock is $\sim$kpc wide, the trail is $\sim 60$ kpc long, and the SMBH apparently moves at $\sim 1,000$ km s$^{-1}$. Using controlled hydrodynamic simulations, we show that the SMBH's gravity alone cannot produce a significant bow shock, but a comoving wind source can sustain one similar to RBH-1's. The wind must either be active or have shut off less than $\sim 3$ Myr ago. The required recent wind momentum flux is $6\times10^{32}\,{\rm dyn}\,(n_{\rm CGM}/10^{-3}\,{\rm cm}^{-3})$, where $n_{\rm CGM}$ is the CGM density. Assuming the wind reaches peak strength only during the last $\sim 6$ Myr, the minimum integrated wind mass is $3.5\times10^5\,M_\odot\,(n_{\rm CGM}/10^{-3}\,{\rm cm}^{-3})$. A $2\times10^7\,M_\odot$ SMBH accreting at $1\%$ Eddington could power the wind. Supernova feedback from a star cluster carried by the SMBH is an alternative, although the required mass and momentum fluxes $\gtrsim 60$ Myr after ejection are difficult to reconcile with a standard initial mass function. For a hot ambient CGM at $\sim 10^6$ K, the quasi-linear trail constrains the 1D velocity dispersion to $σ_{\rm 1D}\lesssim 30$ km s$^{-1}$, above which it becomes strongly disturbed. Runaway SMBH trails therefore offer a new probe of turbulence in the diffuse CGM, in regimes where its kinematics are otherwise inaccessible.

papers.title: ASAS-SN Rates V: Tidal Disruption Event Volumetric Rates and Luminosity Functions by Optical Spectroscopic Type, X-ray Luminosity, and Host-Galaxy Properties
papers.abstract: We present volumetric rates and luminosity functions (LFs) of tidal disruption events (TDEs) based on 21 TDEs from the All-Sky Automated Survey for Supernovae (ASAS-SN) between 2014 and 2024. We calculate completeness corrections from injection-recovery simulations of the ASAS-SN light curves using individual TDE templates. We find a total volumetric rate of $\log_{10}(R_{\rm tot}[{\rm yr}^{-1}{\rm Gpc}^{-3}h_{70}^3]) = 2.32^{+0.15}_{-0.23}$ for $z \leq 0.12$. We also measure the rates of two growing TDE subpopulations. The one off-nuclear TDE in our standard sample implies $\log_{10}(R_{\rm off\text{-}nuclear}) = 0.39^{+0.52}_{-0.76}$ ($1.2^{+3.4}_{-1.0}$% of the total rate). We measure the rate of recurrent TDEs (rTDEs) to be $\log_{10}(R_{\rm recurrent}) = 1.26^{+0.23}_{-0.62}$ ($9^{+8}_{-6}$% of the total rate) from the four rTDEs in our standard sample, increasing to $1.45^{+0.20}_{-0.35}$ ($13^{+10}_{-7}$%) when the well-studied ASASSN-14ko is included. Galaxies with substantial (>0.1%) burst-mass fractions and steeply falling star-formation histories host the majority of TDEs. We recover the known overrepresentation of TDEs in post-starburst galaxies, by a factor of $15^{+16}_{-11}$ relative to matched control galaxies, and a weaker enhancement of $5^{+5}_{-4}$ in quiescent Balmer-strong galaxies. TDE-H+He events dominate the volumetric TDE rate, with TDE-H, TDE-He, and TDE-Featureless events comprising <15% of nearby TDEs. The $g$-band LFs are statistically indistinguishable when split at the median X-ray to UV/optical blackbody luminosity ratio of $\sim$1%, corroborating unification models where the observed multi-wavelength emission is set primarily by viewing angle effects. Extrapolating the measured TDE LFs to higher luminosities and more massive black holes supports a TDE origin for luminous ambiguous nuclear transients and extreme nuclear transients.

papers.title: Supernova Bounds on Neutrino Dipole Moments from a Modern Perspective
papers.abstract: Neutrinos may have nonstandard magnetic dipole moments $μ_ν$. In the dense cores of supernovae (SNe), these would convert part of the neutrinos into sterile, right-handed states through the electromagnetic fluctuations of the charged plasma. The streaming sterile neutrinos with 100-MeV energies can convert back to standard neutrinos in the Galactic magnetic field, leading to a high-energy neutrino flux unobserved from the historical SN 1987A. We reassess the production rates, including scattering on both protons and electrons, and, building upon advances in SN simulations and in the description of the Milky Way magnetic field, we revisit the bounds on magnetic dipole moments. We find for Dirac electron neutrinos $μ_{ν_e} \lesssim 4.8 \times 10^{-13} μ_B$, superseding all existing terrestrial and astrophysical constraints.

papers.title: 21 cm Cosmology of Boosted Dark Matter
papers.abstract: The formation history of low-mass halos is sensitive to the properties of dark matter. At low redshift, nonlinear evolution and baryonic processes can obscure this information. The 21 cm signal provides access to a high-redshift stage of structure formation, when the abundance and clustering of low-mass halos retain direct sensitivity to the mass and interactions of dark matter. Boosted dark matter (BDM) realizes this possibility through a two-component scenario in which the annihilation of the heavier component converts part of the mass difference into kinetic energy of the lighter component. Self-interactions redistribute this energy and generate pressure support, suppressing small-scale density perturbations even for dark matter masses in the MeV range. We calculate the global 21 cm brightness temperature and its power spectrum in BDM cosmology. The reduced abundance of low-mass halos delays the global absorption feature and shifts the characteristic redshift evolution of the power spectrum. We assess the projected sensitivity of SKA1-Low to these signatures. The sensitivity is strongest at intermediate light-component fractions, where both components remain sufficiently abundant for self-heating to affect structure formation. For $σ_{\rm self1}/m_1\simeq0.1\,{\rm cm^2\,g^{-1}}$, models with $0.2\lesssim r_1\lesssim0.7$ can be distinguished from the fiducial $Λ$CDM prediction at the $95\%$ confidence level under the optimistic forecast. We compare our results with existing direct-detection bounds from SENSEI and prospects for BDM searches at large-volume neutrino experiments, including Super-/Hyper-Kamiokande, JUNO, and DUNE. This comparison highlights the unique and complementary role of high-redshift surveys in testing BDM models.

papers.title: Rest-frame annihilation lines of $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in 23,000 stacked galaxy clusters
papers.abstract: Weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) annihilation features were reported as a 43 GeV line in three Fermi-LAT galaxy clusters ($\mathtt{S}_3$), as triad $\{γγ, γZ,γh\}$ lines from $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in LAT data cross-correlated ($\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$) with western eROSITA X-rays, and as a nonad (combining three triads) of two cross-annihilating WIMPs in $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$. A blind scan of LAT 16.3-year data around 23,343 high-latitude clusters in their rest frames finds three triads, at 70 GeV ($2.8σ$ trial-corrected, henceforth), $72$ GeV ($1.3σ$; strengthening to $2.7σ$ if mass-fixed by $\mathtt{S}_3$, $4.0σ$ combined with $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ masked around the clusters, $5.7σ$ if also combined with $\mathtt{S}_3$), and 74-75 GeV: a triplet not only rare ($3.5σ$) but also forming a $\{70,74\}$ GeV nonad ($3.4σ$; strengthening to $4.0σ$, $4.6σ$, and $6.1σ$, respectively). The spectral features, robust in and out of the $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ region and $\mathtt{S}_3$ clusters, appear in all Galactic quadrants and only in the cluster rest frame (vanishing upon redshift rescaling or permutation), fade away from cluster centers, are absent from their surrounding stacked fields, and like $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ indicate intrinsic few $10^{-19}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ cross sections (uncorrected) across samples. All features are largely explained by cross-annihilating $69.7^{+0.4}_{-1.0}$ and $74.5^{+1.1}_{-0.6}$ GeV WIMPs.

papers.title: X-ray Flare Evolution and Changing-Look Nature of the TeV Blazar OQ 334
papers.abstract: The blazar OQ 334 (B2 1420+326, z = 0.682) is one of the few jetted AGN with repeated changing-look (CL) transitions between FSRQ and BL Lac states. We present a multi-wavelength study covering 2017 December to 2024 September, focusing on three X-ray flares observed with Swift-XRT (X1: 2019 June 26--July 24, X2: 2020 January 4--February 21, X3: 2024 June 24--August 2) and on the spectral properties of the CL states. The spectrum hardens from flare to flare, with $Γ$ decreasing from $1.97 \pm 0.09$ to $1.71 \pm 0.04$ and $1.34 \pm 0.06$, while the hysteresis evolves from an initial clockwise loop, consistent with cooling-dominated emission, to multi-loop trajectories in the later flares. The X-ray spectra separate the CL states, with FSRQ states hardest ($Γ_X \approx 1.3$--$1.5$), BL Lac states softest ($Γ_X \approx 1.8$--$2.4$), and transition states intermediate. Within the CL states, flux and photon index are positively correlated ($r = 0.59$, $p = 2.5 \times 10^{-2}$), producing a softer-when-brighter trend. The first two flares coincide with FSRQ $\rightarrow$ BL Lac transitions, whereas the third, the brightest, remains FSRQ-like. One-zone leptonic modelling of the broadband SEDs reproduces the flares with a weak, nearly constant magnetic field and a particle-dominated region, and the X-ray emission evolves from a substantial synchrotron contribution in the first flare to complete inverse-Compton dominance in the third. The X-ray band traces the changing balance between the synchrotron and inverse-Compton components in the flares and provides a sensitive probe of the CL behaviour of the source.

papers.title: Conditions for mass-loading: Investigating jet-disk material exchange in strongly magnetised accretion flows
papers.abstract: Relativistic jets are produced by accreting black holes across a wide range of masses, from stellar-mass X-ray binaries to supermassive active galactic nuclei (AGN). In low-luminosity AGN, these jets are believed to be powered by strongly magnetised accretion flows, a picture supported by Event Horizon Telescope and VLBI observations of M87. The jets often exhibit high-energy flaring emission which, if partly hadronic, implies that baryons must be loaded into the jet and accelerated despite strong magnetic barriers. However, the mechanism behind this remains unclear. We present high-resolution, three-dimensional General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations of a high-spin Magnetically Arrested Disk (MAD), a strongly magnetised accretion regime. Using passive Eulerian tracers, we track the exchange of material between the jet and disk to quantify mixing. We find that magnetic flux eruptions, a hallmark of MAD accretion, expel magnetic flux tubes initially filled with jet material (expected to be pair-dominated in real systems). Through magnetic reconnection during these eruptions, this material is mixed into the disk. Crucially, the same flux tubes reconnect the disk back to the jet, allowing disk material, expected to be primarily hadronic, to infiltrate the jet sheath and boundary. This disk-to-jet injection offers a natural mass-loading mechanism that does not require the jet to be globally baryon-dominated. The resulting ejection-injection cycle may instead drive episodic hadronic acceleration, providing a viable pathway for high-energy emission in relativistic jets.

papers.title: EP241206a: A Sub-kilosecond X-Ray Flare Possibly from an Active Galactic Nucleus with a Flux Increase over 3 Orders of Magnitude
papers.abstract: EP241206a is a fast X-ray transient detected with the Wide-field X-ray Telescope (WXT) on board the Einstein Probe. The event exhibited a single-peaked soft X-ray flare with a duration of $\sim 500$ s and a peak flux of $1.0 \times 10^{-9}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ in 0.5--4 keV, spatially coincident with a spectroscopically confirmed active galactic nucleus (AGN) at $z = 0.62$. Follow-up and archival observations revealed persistent X-ray emission at a level of $\sim 5 \times 10^{-13}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$, corresponding to $L_{2-10 \mathrm{keV}} \simeq 2.3 \times 10^{44}$ erg s$^{-1}$ if associated with the AGN; the WXT flare reached an estimated peak isotropic-equivalent rest-frame 2--10 keV luminosity of $\sim 1.4 \times 10^{48}$ erg s$^{-1}$, implying a peak-to-persistent luminosity contrast of over 3 orders of magnitude. Optical spectroscopy detected broad Mg II and H$β$ emission lines, suggesting a black hole mass of $\sim 3.8 \times 10^{7} M_{\odot}$ and Eddington ratios of 0.8 at the persistent state versus an apparent peak ratio of $\sim 4.6 \times 10^{3}$ during the flare. The extremely short duration and high apparent peak luminosity favor a jet origin, likely due to magnetic reconnection in the inner regions of a relativistic jet. Alternative scenarios include a jet-in-the-jet or a gamma-ray burst occurring within the AGN disk. However, the physical association between the transient and the AGN is not firmly established; for the radio-loud and X-ray-detected AGN counterpart class, the trial-corrected chance probability is $4.9 \times 10^{-3}$. EP241206a may represent an example of a broader population of unidentified fast X-ray transients detected with WXT.

papers.title: Astrophysical Constraints for Bosonic Dark Matter in and Around Quark Stars
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure, stability, and mass-radius relations of compact stars composed of quark matter within the non-ideal MIT Bag Model mixed with self-interacting bosonic dark matter with a $φ^n$ self-interaction potential. By solving the coupled two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations for boson masses between 200 MeV and 1 GeV and self-interaction strengths with $n=4$ and $n=40$, we show that strong self-interactions and higher boson masses enhance the stability of compact star configurations at high central pressures, though they reduce maximum overall masses. Ultra-compact solutions with $C \ge 1/3$ capable of mimicking black holes are significantly restricted compared to hadronic models, emerging only for strong self-interactions and dark matter fractions exceeding 90\%. Depending on the parameters, the compact stars form either extended dark matter halos or compact cores: stronger self-interactions and higher boson masses suppress the radial extension to favor compact cores of dark matter. Matching our models against observational constraints highlights PSR J1614$-$2230 and XTE J1814$-$338 as potential window of opportunity for dark matter detection. Notably, XTE J1814$-$338 could confirm a dark sector, given its requirement for light boson masses ($m_b \approx 200\text{--}300\text{ MeV}$) and strongly DM-dominated configurations.

papers.title: No Supersoft X-rays Before SN 2026ahvu: Constraints on a Potentially Prompt Type Ia Progenitor
papers.abstract: The nearby Type Ia supernova SN 2026ahvu offers a rare opportunity to probe its progenitor that may have evolved unusually rapidly. If the progenitor formed in either of the two young stellar clusters near the explosion site in NGC 1433, the delay from star formation to explosion could have been $\sim$100 Myr or less. The distance to NGC 1433 remains uncertain, with published estimates of 9.1 Mpc and 18.9 Mpc. Our preliminary fit to the rising ATLAS light curve yields a distance of $17.7^{+1.5}_{-1.4}$ Mpc. In the classical single-degenerate scenario, a white dwarf steadily burning hydrogen accreted from a non-degenerate companion can emit detectable supersoft X-rays before explosion. We search for this emission using two archival Chandra observations obtained before the explosion. The observations provide a combined exposure of 95.3 ks, with no 0.3-7 keV photons detected within 2" of the supernova position. For a 100 eV blackbody with Galactic foreground absorption, the 95\% bolometric luminosity limits are $6.3\times10^{37}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and $2.7\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ at 9.1 Mpc and 18.9 Mpc, respectively. At both distances, the observations exclude a hot, compact white dwarf undergoing steady hydrogen burning if the absorption is limited to the Galactic foreground. However, cooler, expanded, or more heavily absorbed photospheres remain viable. Together with the pre-explosion non-detections for SN 2011fe and SN 2014J, our results reinforce the absence of luminous supersoft progenitors in nearby SNe Ia. This pattern is naturally consistent with double-degenerate explosions, although X-ray-faint single-degenerate configurations remain viable. Post-explosion X-ray observations can test for circumstellar interaction and help determine whether material around the progenitor could have obscured a luminous nuclear burning white dwarf.

papers.title: Non-thermal emission from molecular clouds illuminated by continuous cosmic-ray accelerators: application to the stellar cluster W43
papers.abstract: Context: Cosmic rays escaping from their accelerators produce gamma-ray emission through interactions with ambient gas. While the scenario of an impulsive injection of cosmic rays has been extensively studied, that of a continuous injection in time has received comparatively less attention. The latter scenario is particularly relevant for stellar clusters, which may contribute to a non-negligible fraction of Galactic cosmic rays. Aims: We intend to characterize the excesses of cosmic rays around their accelerators and to assess the detectability of the gamma-ray emission resulting from the interactions of cosmic rays in nearby molecular clouds. We focus in particular on star clusters and seek to apply these considerations to the case of W43. Methods: We derive analytical estimates for the cosmic ray excess around sources as a function of source properties and transport parameters. We also evaluate under which conditions the predicted gamma-ray emission from illuminated molecular clouds can be detected by current and future instruments. We then apply these results to explain the gamma-ray emission from the the W43 region. Results: We find that producing detectable gamma-ray emission from molecular clouds illuminated by cosmic rays escaping from star clusters generally requires either suppressed diffusion relative to the Galactic value or anisotropic diffusion, with the latter scenario requiring a smaller global energetic. We applied this approach to the case of W43 and by fitting its gamma-ray emission we were able to constrain the underlying CR transport parameters.

papers.title: Noise and quasi-periodic oscillations in black hole accretion flows
papers.abstract: Temporal fluctuations of the viscosity parameter at different radii in an accretion flow are known to give rise to variability in the accretion rate onto the black hole. The power spectrum of accretion-rate fluctuations is expected to exhibit a broad-band power-law dependence on frequency (e.g., flicker noise). We show that viscosity fluctuations can also generate quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the power spectrum. In our model, QPOs are caused by reflection of accretion-rate fluctuations at the outer radius of the accretion flow and arise near the low-frequency break of the power spectrum, which corresponds to the inverse viscous timescale at the outer radius. These QPOs occur in geometrically thick advection-dominated accretion flows but are absent in geometrically thin cooling-dominated flows.

papers.title: Impact of the Initial Lorentz Factor on Kinetic Instabilities, Magnetic-Field Evolution, and Particle Acceleration in Relativistic Jets
papers.abstract: We investigate how the initial Lorentz factor shapes the evolution of relativistic jets---a key open question in high-energy astrophysics. Using global three-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations with cylindrical jet geometry on a Cartesian grid, we analyze the self-consistent evolution of relativistic electron--positron and electron--ion jets from active galactic nuclei (AGN) and their interaction with the ambient medium. We implement an injection scheme that assigns space- and time-dependent velocities to injected particles and simulate jets with initial Lorentz factors of $γ_{0} = 10$ and 15. Jets with the higher Lorentz factor ($γ_{0} = 15$) exhibit stronger electron collimation, whereas those with $γ_{0} = 10$ show larger growth rates of kinetic instabilities during the linear stage. In both cases, a non-oscillatory electric field accelerates and decelerates charged particles throughout the linear and nonlinear stages. Upon entering the nonlinear regime, the initial toroidal magnetic field undergoes significant amplification driven by the Weibel instability (WI), the kinetic Kelvin--Helmholtz instability (kKHI), and the mushroom instability (MI), and subsequently reorganizes into complex topologies. In the late nonlinear stage, magnetic islands with randomly swirling fields indicate a highly turbulent magnetic structure. These findings demonstrate that global 3D~PIC modeling is essential for capturing the interplay among kinetic instabilities, magnetic turbulence, and particle acceleration in relativistic outflows, bridging microscopic plasma physics with macroscopic observations of AGN jets and gamma-ray bursts.

papers.title: The imprint of neutron escape on non-thermal protons in AGN coronae
papers.abstract: The coronae of active galactic nuclei (AGN) are promising sites of proton acceleration to hundreds of TeV, potentially accounting for the neutrino excess from NGC 1068 reported by IceCube. We show that photohadronic proton-to-neutron conversion provides an important proton escape channel, as neutrons can leave the corona well before decaying. In magnetized turbulent coronae, neutron escape can reduce the characteristic neutrino energy by up to a factor of four and the integrated neutrino luminosity by approximately 30% at a fixed non-thermal proton energy density. More strikingly, proton-to-neutron conversion offers an escape route roughly two orders of magnitude faster than proton diffusion, requiring a correspondingly larger proton injection rate to sustain the non-thermal population. The effect is considerably weaker when proton escape is already ballistic, as expected in magnetic-reconnection scenarios. Therefore, neutron escape is essential for quantitatively connecting neutrino emission from AGN coronae to the efficiency of proton injection into the acceleration process.

papers.title: Maximum entropy reconstruction of the black hole greybody factors from its Korteweg-de Vries integrals
papers.abstract: The dynamics of perturbed non-rotating black holes (BHs) can be described by master wave equations with a potential barrier. Recent work has shown that these equations possess an infinite number of symmetries generated by the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) hierarchy, leading to conserved quantities (KdV integrals) that fully determine the BH greybody factors via a moment problem. In this paper, we introduce and validate a new method to solve this moment problem using the maximum entropy principle. The method reconstructs, at each order of truncation, the least-biased transmission probability compatible with a finite set of KdV integrals, guaranteeing positivity by construction. We first validate the technique against the exactly solvable Pöschl-Teller potential. We then apply it to the Regge-Wheeler potential governing axial perturbations of a Schwarzschild BH, where no exact solution is available; the resulting reconstruction agrees closely with the fourth-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation across several multipoles. This is the first application of the maximum entropy method to the reconstruction of BH greybody factors, demonstrating that a modest number of KdV integrals is sufficient to recover them accurately.

papers.title: Linear Electrostatic Instabilities Driven by Relativistic Non-Maxwellian Pair Beams
papers.abstract: We investigate how non-Maxwellian momentum distributions affect the linear growth of electrostatic instabilities driven by relativistic pair beams, motivated by the lack of a universally accepted analytical description of blazar-induced pair beams. Different beam distributions are used to describe relativistic pair beams in analytical studies and particle-in-cell simulations. A systematic comparison is therefore needed to determine how the beam distribution influences the instability growth rates. We formulate the relativistic electrostatic response in the weak-beam limit for an anisotropic $κ$-type distribution and compare the resulting growth rates with those obtained for Gaussian and Maxwell--Jüttner distributions. We require $κ>3/2$ for a finite root-mean-square momentum spread. For the parameters considered, the $κ$-type distributions yield higher maximum growth rates than the Gaussian distribution, even when their mean momenta and momentum spreads are the same. The fastest-growing modes correspond to parallel propagation for the $κ$ and Gaussian distributions, whereas the Maxwell--Jüttner distribution exhibits its maximum for oblique propagation for a mildly relativistic beam. An additional calculation for a highly relativistic pair beam with $κ=2$ finds an oblique maximum of the electrostatic growth rate. The beam momentum distribution influences the linear growth of electrostatic instabilities under the conditions investigated.

papers.title: AstroSat Observations of Stellar Mass Black Hole X-ray Binaries: Towards a Unified Accretion Disc Configuration
papers.abstract: We present spectro-temporal review of $34$ black hole X-ray binaries (BH-XRBs), classified as persistent-cum-variable, persistent and transient, observed with \textit{AstroSat} during its first decade of operations. Using over $12$ Ms of data, wide-band multi-wavelength coverage in UV/Optical and X-rays, and $\sim10\,μ\text{s}$ temporal resolution, we probe accretion-ejection dynamics in strong gravity. LFQPOs ($0.1-8.0\text{ Hz}$) are detected across several sources, exceeding $40\text{ keV}$ in MAXI J1535$-$571 and H 1743$-$322, while Swift J1727.8$-$1613 exhibits the first detection of LFQPOs up to $100$ keV, indicating the dominant Comptonized emission. In GRS 1915$+$105, we identify a new variability class ($τ$), expanding known classes to fifteen, and detect $\sim70\text{ Hz}$ HFQPOs in the $γ$, $κ$, $δ$, $ω$, and $τ$ classes, implying a `compact' oscillating corona within $\lesssim 10\,r_g$. Among persistent sources, we report the first detections of a type-A LFQPO ($\sim2.7\text{ Hz}$) in 4U 1957$+$11 and type-B LFQPOs ($4-8\text{ Hz}$) in 4U 1630$-$472. Broadband thermal disc along with Comptonization modelling reveals tight correlations among QPO frequency, time-lag, rms variability, photon index ($Γ_{\rm th}$), disc-to-Comptonized flux ratio ($F_{\rm ratio}$), and bolometric luminosity ($L_{\rm bol}$), tracing disc-corona-jet coupling and identifying `canonical' spectral states (LHS, HIMS, SIMS, HSS). Type-C QPOs exhibit soft-lags with occasional reversals at high coronal fractions ($>0.8$), whereas type-B QPOs show hard-lags at lower fractions ($<0.5$), linking to disc-jet coupling. Supported by simulations and radiation driven spectral modelling, these results favor a unified accretion framework while outlining limitations, challenges and future prospects.

papers.title: A 3+1 formalism for self-similar expanding grids in computational relativistic and Newtonian magnetohydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Astrophysical systems frequently undergo spatial expansion during their evolution. Simulating these systems with standard conservative codes for hydrodynamics and magnetohydrodynamics using fixed grids is challenging, particularly when attempting to preserve high resolution across vast changes in physical scale. While moving or expanding meshes, or adapting mesh refinement, can address this issue, they introduce computational complexity and are notoriously difficult to implement robustly. We aim to overcome these barriers by providing an easily implementable strategy that empowers the community to achieve high-fidelity results and establishes expanding-grid approaches as a highly accessible standard practice. Leveraging the gauge freedom of the 3+1 formalism for MHD on curved manifolds, a foundation common to all general relativistic fluid dynamics codes, we demonstrate how an expanding coordinate system can be implemented purely through a simple modification of the underlying metric. This requires zero modifications to the numerical mesh or the core structure of the code, and the necessary addition or modification of metric terms can be easily accomplished even in Newtonian MHD. We apply this framework to standard test problems in both relativistic and Newtonian hydrodynamics and MHD, directly comparing the results of fixed and expanding coordinates. Our tests demonstrate the full consistency, accuracy, and robustness of this metric-based expansion approach, as the original conservative formulations is fully preserved. Through a simple coordinate transformation and a re-definition of the metric tensor, any general relativistic MHD code can be effortlessly transformed into an expanding-grid code. This approach elegantly guarantees both fundamental conservation properties and the solenoidal condition for the magnetic field, and can be readily extended to include non-ideal effects.

papers.title: Simultaneous tests of post-Newtonian inspiral using GW250114 and GW250207
papers.abstract: We perform the one of the most general tests of post-Newtonian (PN) inspiral in binary black holes to date by allowing all eight phase coefficients up to 3.5PN order to vary simultaneously from their general-relativistic values. Using two of the loudest binary black hole events observed to date, GW250114 and GW250207, we carry out Bayesian inference with the IMRPhenomXPHM_SpinTaylor waveform model augmented by parametrized deviations in the post-Newtonian phasing. We then identify the combinations of phase coefficients most strongly constrained by the data through a principal component analysis of the eight-dimensional deformation space. We find that the data constrain the three leading principal components beyond their priors, and that all three are consistent with the predictions of general relativity. These results demonstrate that exceptionally loud gravitational-wave events enable robust, high-dimensional tests of inspiral dynamics and provide direct access to the measurable subspace of post-Newtonian deformations.

papers.title: The Effect of Asphericity to the Inference of Supernova Circumstellar Environment from Radio Observations
papers.abstract: Radio observations of supernovae (SNe) enable us to constrain the circumstellar environment of their progenitor stars, and hence the mass-loss history immediately prior to the explosion. However, despite lines of evidence pointing to the aspherical configurations of circumstellar matter (CSM) around many SNe, the derivation of CSM parameters is often done under the assumption of spherically symmetric CSM. In this work, based on a recent model of radio emission from SNe interacting with aspherical CSM, we investigate how lifting the assumption of spherical symmetry affects the CSM parameter inference. First, we apply the model to mock data simulating typical observations of Type Ia-CSM, Ibc and II SNe and find that the total CSM mass required for to reproduce radio observation depends weakly on the CSM covering fraction $f_Ω$, with ${f_Ω}^{0.15-0.38}$. We then apply the model and fit the radio light curves of Type Ia-CSM SN 2020eyj. We show that, even with the assumption of asphericity as severe as $f_Ω= 0.1$, the requirement for the total CSM mass is only reduced to $\sim 50 \%$ of the value inferred in spherical models. These results demonstrate that introducing asphericity in radio emission models is often not enough to reduce the required CSM mass significantly.

papers.title: Long-Term Radio Evolution of the Type Ia Supernova SN 2020eyj: Evidence for a Dense Helium-rich Circumstellar Shell
